sections.title: Molecular profile of uterine serous carcinoma
sections.intro: Serous is the most molecularly homogeneous endometrial histotype — the classifier's poor-prognosis group was named after it.

cols.regimen: Doxorubicin 60 + cisplatin 50 q3w ×7 (+1 cisplatin) vs whole-abdominal RT
Vaginal cuff brachytherapy → carbo AUC6 + paclitaxel 175 ×3 vs pelvic RT 45–50.4 Gy
cols.pop: High-intermediate/high-risk **early stage**: stage I endometrioid (GOG-33 HIR criteria), stage II, or **stage I–II serous / clear cell**
cols.hist: **15% serous** (endometrioid 71%, CC 5%); high-risk-histology cohort showed **no benefit** from added chemo (serous/CC RFS HR 0.81, 0.44–1.52); trial-wide **worse nodal control** (pelvic/PA recurrence 9% vs 4%)

cols.regimen: Cisplatin 50 D1/D29 + 45 Gy → carbo/taxol ×4 vs carbo/taxol ×6
cols.pop: Stage III/IVA; also stage I/II serous or CC with +washings
HER2+ serous or carcinosarcoma, IA–IVB non-recurrent

notes.title: GOG-258 is the only adjuvant trial that enters serous by histology rather than by chance — stage I/II serous with positive peritoneal washings was an explicit eligibility route (<3% of cohort).
notes.md: GY026 enrols stage I–IV non-recurrent, so its stage III–IV patients overlap Table 2. It is the trial that will settle HER2-directed therapy in this histology.

sections.title: 2. Primary systemic therapy (first-line, chemo-naive advanced)
sections.intro: The three classic GOG trials (GOG-107, -177, -209) enrolled advanced **and** recurrent patients in one population, so each is listed here **and** in Table 3 — marked ↔ T3 / ↔ T2. They are the same rows, not different analyses; the recurrent fraction of each is given in Table 3. GOG-177 is in fact majority-recurrent (58–71%), so treating it as a purely advanced-disease trial would misread it.

cols.regimen: Carbo/taxol + trastuzumab → T maintenance vs carbo/taxol
Same ×6 → durvalumab 1500 mg q4w **+ olaparib 300 mg BID** maintenance vs carbo/taxol
cols.hist: Same cohort; serous progression **24/42 (57.1%)** vs 79.6% control; **HR 0.46 (0.27–0.77)**, exploratory (Fig 3B)

cols.regimen: Carbo AUC5–6/taxol 175 + durvalumab 1120 mg ×6 → durvalumab 1500 mg q4w maintenance vs carbo/taxol
cols.pop: Newly dx **measurable** III/IV **or recurrent** (52% recurrent); prior adjuvant chemo allowed if DFI ≥12 mo
cols.hist: **21.5% serous (154/718)**; serous **is** a forest-plot subgroup — progression **43/54 (79.6%) control → 41/58 (70.7%)**; HR 0.71 (0.46–1.11), exploratory (Fig 3A)
cols.os: interim (28% mat.) HR 0.77 (0.56–1.07), NS; control median OS 25.9 mo

cols.regimen: TAP (dox 45 D1 + cis 50 D1 + paclitaxel 160 D2 + filgrastim D3–12) vs AP
Doxorubicin 60 + cisplatin 50 q3w vs doxorubicin 60 alone
Carbo AUC5–6 + paclitaxel 175 + atezolizumab 1200 mg ×6–8 → atezo maintenance vs placebo
cols.pop: Advanced or recurrent EC **or carcinosarcoma**; ≤1 prior platinum line ≥6 mo prior
cols.hist: **88/549 serous (16%)**; exploratory PFS subgroup 47/59 vs 23/29 events, HR 0.87 (0.52–1.45), not preplanned (Fig 4B)
cols.pfs: ITT 10.1 vs 8.9 mo; dMMR NE vs 6.9 mo; **pMMR 9.5 vs 9.2 mo**
cols.os: ITT 36.0 vs 30.5 mo (ESMO 2025, median f/u 48.9 mo) — **not significant**

cols.hist: 19.7% serous (262); exploratory OS HR 1.20 (0.91–1.59), TC vs TAP (Fig 4)

notes.title: Two interpretation traps
notes.md:
- **GOG-209 established carbo/taxol by non-inferiority, not superiority.** Do not read 37 vs 41 mo as favouring carbo/taxol.
- **GOG-177 is the one informative pre-molecular serous signal.** Adding paclitaxel to AP lifted response from 33%→59% in non-serous histologies but only 42%→50% in serous. Small numbers, but an early hint that USC responds differently on the same backbone — consistent with everything since.

sections.title: 3. Recurrent disease
sections.intro: Recurrent disease is **not one setting**. The GOG trials treated recurrence with first-line cytotoxic therapy in patients who had never had chemotherapy; the modern trials treat recurrence after platinum and, increasingly, after a checkpoint inhibitor. These populations are not interchangeable and their numbers must not be read across. Table 3 is therefore split by **line of therapy**, not by "recurrent" as a label.

notes.title: Why this split exists
notes.md: GOG-107, GOG-177 and GOG-209 all **excluded prior cytotoxic chemotherapy** (radiosensitisation excluded). Their recurrent patients were chemo-naive and received a platinum or anthracycline doublet as their *first* systemic therapy. Reading AP, TAP or carbo/taxol medians from 3A as salvage-line expectations will overestimate what a pretreated patient can expect — the GOG-209 subgroup data make the gap explicit: median OS 20.4–22.0 months in measurable/recurrent patients versus 113 months in the non-measurable, non-recurrent group of the same trial.

cols.pop: ≤3 prior chemo allowed; median 1 prior line (0–2)

cols.regimen: Doxorubicin 60 + cisplatin 50 q3w vs doxorubicin 60 alone

cols.os: 37 vs 41 mo overall; **measurable/recurrent subgroup 20.4 (TC) vs 22.0 (TAP) mo**

cols.regimen: Lenvatinib 20 mg + pembrolizumab vs doxorubicin or wkly paclitaxel
Sac-TMT 4 mg/kg q2w vs doxorubicin or paclitaxel

cols.tox: **No 2L trial data.** Use is extrapolated from GOG-209, a **chemo-naive** trial (row in 3A)

notes.title: Reading notes
notes.md:
- The n = 17 Fader recurrent subgroup shows why `n` earns its column: a PFS HR of 0.12 with no OS separation should not be read as a large effect.
- The platinum-re-treatment row is deliberately marked ⚠️. It is the one place in this file where a widely used clinical practice rests on extrapolation across the 3A/3B boundary rather than on data generated in the 3B population.
- Hormonal options (GOG-81 MPA, tamoxifen) are omitted: USC is typically ER/PR-low, so they would be filler here rather than options.
